platform: macOS aarch64 local white-box reproduction cross-checked by an isolated OpenJDK JVM fixture
trigger: an interface method reference names clone(), the current interface no longer declares it, java.lang.Object exposes only protected clone(), and the concrete implementation still has a public clone() method
actual_pre_fix_behavior: both the runtime reconciler and the independent validation oracle recursively traversed an interface classfile's java/lang/Object super_name and accepted protected, private, or static Object declarations as ordinary inherited interface methods
expected_behavior: JVMS interface method resolution may use a java.lang.Object fallback only when that declaration is public and non-static; otherwise resolution must continue through superinterfaces and fail when no legal declaration exists
root_cause: the shared conceptual model treated the synthetic Object superclass recorded on an interface classfile as a normal superclass edge instead of applying the interface-specific Object fallback constraints
reproduction: Compile a base interface that explicitly declares Object clone() and a business entrypoint whose bytecode uses invokeinterface for that symbol.
Remove clone() from the current interface while retaining public clone() on the concrete implementation.
Run the same business and oracle classes with the base and current libraries; the base succeeds and the current target JVM raises NoSuchMethodError.
Cross-check javap public-member inventory and require the public binary pipeline to report the removed reachable interface method as incompatible.
